# Add a DLC to test the pack unlock and import

**Headline:** Ship a real, production residential-themed card pack (~10 balanced
cards with bespoke art) for Main Street, gated behind the launcher's unified
content-unlock store, with a scoped simulated-purchase flow that proves the
end-to-end pack **unlock → import** path.

## Problem statement

The card-pack DLC channel (merge, persistence and in-game listing) has shipped,
but there is no real Main Street pack exercising the **unlock → import** path
end-to-end, and no pack gated by the launcher's unified content-unlock store.
Without committed pack content plus a simulated purchase, the DLC feature cannot
be demonstrated or regression-tested beyond in-memory stubs.

## Users

- **Main Street player** — unlocks the residential pack and sees its new cards
  dealt into play.
  - *As a player, I want to buy/unlock a residential card pack and have its
    cards appear in my pool, so new content extends the game.*
  - *As a player, I want a locked pack to stay out of play until I own it, so
    gated content is respected.*
- **Developer / QA** — uses the simulated purchase to verify the whole channel.
  - *As a QA engineer, I want to simulate a pack purchase without a real
    storefront, so I can test lock → unlock → enable → deal → save/load.*
- **Producer** — demonstrates the DLC channel with real, shippable content.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A production pack source tree exists under a new top-level `packs/` directory
   (`manifest.json` + `main-street/main-street-residential-pack/` CSV fragment +
   art), reuses Main Street's `card-data.csv` header **exactly**, has unique card
   ids, and builds cleanly with the core card-pack builder into an installable
   `<contentDir>/packs/` root.
2. The pack adds roughly ten new **residential-themed** cards spanning the
   families (business, event, upgrade, staff, community-space); each row follows
   the existing tier/cost/effect conventions and the set passes the
   balance/catalogue checks.
3. Every new card has bespoke project-generated art in `src/sprites/` and
   resolves to dedicated (non-`Fallback`) art through the regenerated
   `card-art-map.json`.
4. The pack is gated on the unified content-unlock store: while locked its cards
   stay out of play; a scoped simulated purchase (no collateral unlock, state
   persists across restarts) makes it show as unlocked in the Card Packs
   listing, enable-able, merged into the pool, and its cards deal in play.
5. Saves that record the active residential pack restore the same pool on load,
   and a missing/disabled pack degrades gracefully (warn, base content).
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Test Plan

- **Unit / content** — pack manifest + CSV validity (exact base header, unique
  ids, family coverage), and balance/catalogue checks over the new rows.
- **Unit / pipeline** — pack gate resolves the pack as locked with no unlock and
  as entitled once a `dlc:main-street:main-street-residential-pack` unlock
  exists; `loadMainStreetCardPacks` merges the residential rows and the pool
  applies; save/load round-trips the active pack + merged checksum; missing-pack
  degradation.
- **Unit / unlock scope** — the simulated purchase unlocks only the residential
  pack and does **not** unlock the configured itch.io golf reward.
- **Browser / UI** — the Card Packs listing shows the pack locked, the simulated
  purchase flips it to unlocked, and it can then be enabled.
- **Art** — the runtime resolver and the static SVG generator agree that each
  new card resolves to dedicated art (mirrors the existing art-agreement test).

## Constraints

- **Cross-repo surface.** The Main Street pack gate can consume the unified
  store through the existing `CardPackLoaderOptions.resolveEntitlement` seam
  (Main Street side), but the *write* path (a reward rule/verifier simulating the
  purchase) lives in the core launcher. Any core change must be committed to the
  `./core` submodule and the submodule bumped in the same work-item, as previous
  cross-repo items did.
- **Global attestation side effect.** `contentUnlocks.refresh({ attested: true })`
  self-attests *every* configured rule, which would also unlock the itch.io golf
  reward. The simulated purchase must scope verification to the residential pack
  (a `(platform, action)`-keyed verifier or equivalent rule-scoped mechanism).
- **Pack merge rules.** The fragment must reuse the base header exactly;
  duplicate ids or a mismatched header reject the pack whole (core contract).
- **Art.** Art must be project-generated, deterministic/reproducible, and
  licence-clean (CC0 / in-house), matching the existing 1024×1024 source-sprite
  pipeline.
- **Additive only.** No changes to base card data or balance; the pack is purely
  additive.
- **Push policy.** Commit/push to `dev` only, never `main`.

## Existing state

- Card-pack channel complete and shipped: `src/MainStreetCardPacks.ts`
  (merge/persistence, one entry point), `MS-0MV07GNUU005E536`; listing UI/boot
  wiring, `MS-0MV0OK0XU0062E0H`; e2e pipeline test, `MS-0MV0Q479I002W0R6`; docs
  cross-reference, `MS-0MV0R1H5S007TTVG`.
- Core pack contract/loader/merge/entitlement and the reference pack live under
  `core/`: `core/src/core-engine/CardPackManifest.ts`,
  `core/src/ui/CardPackLoader.ts` (with a `resolveEntitlement` seam),
  `core/electron/card-pack-entitlements.ts` (Steam-DLC shaped) and
  `core/tests/fixtures/reference-packs/main-street/` (3-card
  `main-street-foundations`).
- Unified content-unlock store shipped in core: `core/electron/action-rewards.ts`
  (+ `FileContentUnlockStore`), `core/electron/action-verifiers.ts`,
  `core/electron/action-rewards.json`, renderer read client
  `core/src/ui/content-unlock-client.ts`, and the pure gate
  `core/src/core-engine/DlcGate.ts`.
- The card-pack gate does **not** currently consult `contentUnlocks`; the loader
  resolves entitlement through the Steam-DLC-shaped `cardPackClient`
  (`entitlement.steamAppId` / the DLC catalog placeholder
  `main-street-founders-pack → app 480`).
- Card art is a generated build artefact:
  `src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` builds `src/card-art-map.json`
  from `src/sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` + `src/card-data.csv`.
- `core/scripts/build-card-pack.mjs` (core `build:card-pack` npm script) turns a
  pack source tree into an installable `<contentDir>/packs/` root.

## Desired change

1. **Pack content** — author a new production pack source tree under `packs/`:
   `packs/manifest.json` declaring `main-street-residential-pack`
   (`gameId: main-street`, version, `coreEngineVersion`, `cards`, `assets`);
   `packs/main-street/main-street-residential-pack/cards.csv` with ~10
   residential-theme cards in the base schema; and
   `packs/main-street/main-street-residential-pack/assets/*.png` pack art. Add a
   Main Street npm script wrapper for the core builder so the build is
   reproducible, and install under `<contentDir>/packs/`.
2. **Art** — generate bespoke 1024×1024 source sprites for the new cards into
   `src/sprites/`, regenerate `src/card-art-map.json`, and (if needed) extend the
   art generator so pack cards are mapped/covered.
3. **Unlock gate** — compose Main Street's pack entitlement resolution so a
   `dlc:main-street:main-street-residential-pack` content-unlock (via
   `contentUnlockClientFromWindow`) entitles the pack in addition to the existing
   Steam-DLC status.
4. **Simulated purchase** — add a scoped simulated-purchase reward rule/verifier
   in the core launcher targeting that DLC id, and a dev/QA affordance (for
   example a control in the Card Packs listing) that performs the purchase and
   refreshes the pack pool.
5. **Tests + docs** — cover content validity, the unlock/import pipeline and the
   listing behaviour (per Test Plan); update `README.md`, `src/README.md`,
   `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` and add a pack `README.md`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packs/manifest.json` — New pack catalogue entry for `main-street-residential-pack`.
- `packs/main-street/main-street-residential-pack/cards.csv` — New ~10-card residential fragment.
- `packs/main-street/main-street-residential-pack/assets/` — New pack art assets.
- `packs/README.md` — New: authoring/installing the production pack.
- `src/MainStreetCardPacks.ts` — Compose content-unlock entitlement into the loader seam.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — Simulated-purchase affordance in the Card Packs panel.
- `src/sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` — New bespoke source sprites (one per new card).
- `src/card-art-map.json` — Regenerated art map covering the new cards.
- `src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` — Extend to include pack card art.
- `package.json` — Add a `build:card-pack` wrapper invoking the core builder.
- `core/electron/action-rewards.json` — Add the scoped residential-pack purchase rule.
- `core/electron/action-verifiers.ts` — (If required) a `(platform, action)`-scoped simulated-purchase verifier.
- `tests/main-street/` — Pack content, unlock/import and listing tests.
- `README.md`, `src/README.md`, `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` — Docs updates.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — art-generator gap.** There is no committed generator for the source
  `*_1024_x_1024.png` sprites; producing ten bespoke sprites reproducibly may
  need a new deterministic generator script. *Mitigation:* author a small
  generator (SVG→PNG via the existing `sharp` dependency) and commit it.
- **Risk — cross-repo change.** The unlock write-path config/verifier is in the
  core launcher; this requires a core commit + submodule bump. *Mitigation:* keep
  the core change minimal and config/verifier-scoped; record both commits.
- **Risk — global attestation.** `refresh({attested:true})` unlocks every rule.
  *Mitigation:* scope the verifier to `(platform, action)` so only the purchase
  rule verifies.
- **Risk — balance.** Monte Carlo / guardrail checks can be slow or flaky.
  *Mitigation:* size the set with the balance tool and catalogue checks; run the
  guardrails once at the end.
- **Risk — packaging.** The new `packs/` tree must reach the built artefact /
  content directory. *Mitigation:* document and wire the install step; verify
  with the e2e pipeline test.
- **Risk — scope creep.** Storyline/tier integration, extra cards or a full
  storefront purchase are out of scope. *Mitigation:* record them as linked
  follow-up work items, not scope.
- **Assumption — identifiers.** Pack id / DLC id / `dlcId` =
  `main-street-residential-pack`; `gameId` = `main-street`.
- **Assumption — card count.** "~10" cards; 8–12 acceptable if required for
  balance and family coverage.
- **Assumption — simulated payment.** A dev/QA-only simulated purchase, not a
  real storefront transaction.
- **Assumption — art licence.** All generated art is project-owned (CC0),
  matching the existing sprite provenance.

## Related work

- `Main Street pack merge & persistence` — `MS-0MV07GNUU005E536` (done): the
  single merge entry point and save/load persistence this pack flows through.
- `Main Street pack listing UI & boot wiring` — `MS-0MV0OK0XU0062E0H` (done):
  the Card Packs listing and boot discovery the unlock affordance extends.
- `End-to-end card-pack pipeline integration test` — `MS-0MV0Q479I002W0R6`
  (done): the loader → merge → save/load test the pack can be added to.
- `Documentation: Main Street card packs (DLC) cross-reference` —
  `MS-0MV0R1H5S007TTVG` (done): docs this item updates.
- Core DLC epic `CG-0MUZFD1WR0031QTB` and the unified content-unlock feature
  `CG-0MUZF156A007OUIT` (referenced via the `./core` submodule).

### Related work (automated report)

Generated by `/skill:find-related` (keywords: dlc, pack, unlock, cards,
residential, create, mechanism, test, …).

**Related work items**
- **MS-0MV0OK0XU0062E0H** – Main Street pack listing UI & boot wiring (completed)
- **MS-0MUOLL8W2004A3D7** – Serial Seller: achievement manifest entry + Steamworks API name (open) — *low relevance (keyword noise)*
- **MS-0MUYGX03R008FZR2** – Update documentation and code comments for new cost values (completed) — *low relevance (keyword noise)*

**Repository file matches**
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — Card Packs contract/builder/entitlement reference.
- `core/docs/the-build/engine-capabilities-audit.md`
- `core/AGENTS.md`

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Which is the target pack artefact and where should its content live —
  (A) a new `main-street-residential-pack` under the reference fixture, (B)
  reuse `main-street-founders-pack`/app 480, or (C) production content under a
  new top-level `packs/` directory?" — Answer (rgardler): **C — production
  content under a new top-level `packs/` directory**. Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "How should the simulated payment work — (A) a dev-only Unlock/Buy
  affordance in the Card Packs listing granting the entitlement, (B) an
  npm/CLI grant script, (C) reuse the existing `contentUnlocks` mechanism, or
  (D) an in-game economy purchase?" — Answer (rgardler): **C — reuse the
  existing contentUnlocks mechanism**. Research: the pack gate
  (`core/src/ui/CardPackLoader.ts`) resolves entitlement through the Steam-DLC
  shaped `cardPackClient` and does **not** consult `contentUnlocks`; the
  renderer exposes only `isUnlocked`/`getUnlocks`/`refresh` (no direct write),
  so the purchase must be a configured reward rule driven through
  `contentUnlocks.refresh`. Source: interactive reply + repo inspection.
- Q: "What is the card-set scope — (A) functional cards with placeholder art,
  or (B) a balance-tuned set plus bespoke generated art?" — Answer (rgardler):
  **B — balance-tuned set, bespoke generated art, ~10 cards (can be more or
  less as necessary for balance)**. Source: interactive reply.
- Q (round 2): "Describe the differences/pros/cons of the content-unlock (C)
  vs the dev-entitlement (A) purchase simulation." — Answer (rgardler): **chose
  C**. Source: interactive reply.

## Out of scope

- Real storefront/Steam purchase wiring.
- Storyline, tier/meta-progression or challenge integration for the new cards.
- Rebalancing the base card pool.
- Additional packs beyond the residential set.


## Plan: changelog

- **2026-10-09** — `plan` session (`herdr-1791563523-3083199-21181`) decomposed this item into **10 children** (3 verification, 6 implementation/docs, 1 release verification). Pre-check decision `plan` (effort Medium, risk High); approval gate **not** required (only Extra-Large effort **and** High/Severe risk pause for producer approval). Verification children were **created first** (test-first creation order) with dependency edges pointing verification → implementation so each suite runs green once its code lands. AC-coverage review recommendation: `proceed` (all seven parent ACs are covered by at least one child; see the mapping below).

### Children

| # | ID | Type | Title | Depends on |
|---|----|------|-------|------------|
| 1 | MS-0MV16VX310089U2L | task | Verification: residential pack content & builder contract | F4 |
| 2 | MS-0MV16VXDZ007NBK8 | task | Verification: residential pack art coverage | F5 |
| 3 | MS-0MV16VXPV002JVX5 | task | Verification: pack unlock, purchase & save/load pipeline | F4, F6, F7, F8 |
| 4 | MS-0MV16VY0U0024E4T | feature | Production residential pack content & builder wrapper | — |
| 5 | MS-0MV16VYC20078A36 | feature | Bespoke residential pack art & generator coverage | F4 |
| 6 | MS-0MV16VYN3006SWM4 | feature | Content-unlock pack entitlement gate | — |
| 7 | MS-0MV16VYYB000TI7H | feature | Scoped simulated purchase in the core launcher | — |
| 8 | MS-0MV16VZ9R008XTF5 | feature | Card Packs listing simulated-purchase affordance | F6, F7 |
| 9 | MS-0MV16VZLH007N4PC | docs | Documentation updates for the residential pack | F4–F8 |
| 10 | MS-0MV16VZWP001OUNR | task | Full-suite verification & release readiness | T1–T3, D9 |

### Parent AC → child coverage

- **AC1** (pack source tree, exact header, unique ids, builder) → F4 + T1.
- **AC2** (~10 residential cards across families, balance/catalogue) → F4 + T1.
- **AC3** (bespoke art in `src/sprites/`, dedicated non-`Fallback` map) → F5 + T2.
- **AC4** (gated on the unified content-unlock store; scoped simulated purchase; listing; deal in play) → F6, F7, F8 + T3.
- **AC5** (save/load restores the pack; missing/disabled degrades) → F6 + T3.
- **AC6** (all related documentation) → D9.
- **AC7** (full suite passes) → T10.

### Phasing

Implemented as independently verifiable slices: content/build → art → gate → scoped purchase → listing → docs → full-suite verification. Each slice carries its own automated coverage; the three `Verification:` children are the dedicated acceptance suites for content/builder, art coverage, and the unlock/purchase/save-load pipeline. Between phases, re-read the next child's description and update it with anything learned (the plan is intentionally a living artefact until each child is implemented).


### Appendix revision (plan session)

No new clarifying questions were asked: the intake Appendix above already resolves the pack-location question (C — production content under a new top-level `packs/`), the simulated-payment question (C — reuse the existing `contentUnlocks` mechanism) and the card-set-scope question (B — balance-tuned set, bespoke generated art, ~10 cards). The plan therefore re-uses those answers and records the following documented assumptions and design decisions rather than re-asking:

- **Gating declaration.** The residential pack is gated on the launcher's unified content-unlock store. The read side composes a `dlc:main-street:main-street-residential-pack` unlock at the `CardPackLoaderOptions.resolveEntitlement` seam *in addition to* the existing Steam-DLC status. Which packs are content-unlock gated is a data-driven declaration (proposed: an additive entitlement marker surfaced on `CardPackStatusRef`, parsed by the core manifest/loader). A simpler equivalent that preserves the same behaviour is acceptable — the implementer records the final shape in the work item.
- **Scoped purchase.** The write path adds an additive rule-scope filter and an explicit simulated-purchase signal to `ActionRewardService.refresh` (and the `contentUnlocks:refresh` IPC/preload/renderer-client chain) plus a `SimulatedPurchase` verifier. This is the "equivalent rule-scoped mechanism" that prevents `refresh({ attested: true })` from collateral-unlocking anything, and prevents the scoped purchase from unlocking the `itchio-follow` golf reward.
- **Art.** Card-face art lives at `src/sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` and is covered by the regenerated `src/card-art-map.json`; a new deterministic generator is required because no committed source-sprite generator exists. Pack `assets/` are separate pack art files.
- **Identifiers (from intake).** pack id / DLC id = `main-street-residential-pack`; `gameId` = `main-street`; unlock target key = `dlc:main-street:main-street-residential-pack`; proposed dev/QA trigger `(platform: dev, action: simulate-purchase)` and rule id `main-street-residential-pack-purchase`.
- **Test-first ordering.** Verification children are created before implementation children; dependency edges point verification → implementation so each verification suite runs green once the code lands (the TDD red→green cycle executes inside the implementation child).
- **No invented requirements.** Storyline/tier integration, a real storefront purchase and extra packs remain out of scope per the parent's "Out of scope" section.

# Verification: residential pack content & builder contract

**Summary:** Author the automated verification that the production residential pack source tree, its CSV fragment and the builder output satisfy the pack contract and the balance/catalogue checks.

**Parent:** MS-0MV0M5BHH0020WFY (Add a DLC to test the pack unlock and import).

## Scope

- Read the real authored pack tree (`packs/manifest.json`, `packs/main-street/main-street-residential-pack/cards.csv`) — not fixtures.
- Drive the real core builder (`core/scripts/build-card-pack.mjs`) and the real merge seam (`mergeCardPackCsv`).
- Assert the content is shippable and additive; this item authors tests only (no game code).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A Vitest unit suite parses `packs/manifest.json` and asserts it declares the `main-street-residential-pack` entry with `gameId: main-street`, a version, a `coreEngineVersion` range, a `cards` path and its `assets`.
- The suite asserts the pack CSV header equals Main Street's `src/card-data.csv` header **exactly** (same columns, same order), that every new card id is unique, and that no new id/name collides with the base pool.
- The suite asserts the pack adds 8–12 residential-themed cards spanning the families (business, event, upgrade, staff, community-space) and that the rows follow the existing tier/cost/effect conventions.
- The suite runs `core/scripts/build-card-pack.mjs --input packs` into a temp directory and asserts the emitted `<out>/manifest.json` + `<out>/main-street/main-street-residential-pack/cards.csv` parse and merge with the base pool via `mergeCardPackCsv` with **no conflicts and no errors**.
- The suite runs the existing schema/balance/catalogue checks over `base + pack` rows and asserts they pass (no invented balance requirements).
- The suite is expected to be red until the pack-content child lands, then green with no further test edits.

## Minimal Implementation

- New `tests/main-street/ResidentialPackContent.test.ts`.
- Reuse the header/CSV parsing helpers already exercised by `tests/main-street/CardPackPipelineIntegration.test.ts`; import the core builder through the `@core-scripts/*` alias.
- Materialise builder output in an `os.tmpdir()` directory and clean up in `afterEach`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `tests/main-street/ResidentialPackContent.test.ts` — New.
- `packs/manifest.json`, `packs/main-street/main-street-residential-pack/cards.csv` — Read (authored by the pack-content child).
- `core/scripts/build-card-pack.mjs`, `core/src/core-engine/CardPackMerge.ts`, `core/src/core-engine/CardPackManifest.ts` — Read.
- `src/card-data.csv` — Base header/id source of truth.

## Dependencies

- Depends on **Production residential pack content & builder wrapper** (verifies its output).
- No new production code beyond the test file.

## Deliverables

- A committed, green (after the content child) verification suite and the documented command to run it.

# Verification: residential pack art coverage

**Summary:** Author the automated verification that every residential pack card resolves to dedicated (non-`Fallback`) bespoke art in `src/sprites/` through the regenerated `card-art-map.json`, and that the runtime and static art paths agree.

**Parent:** MS-0MV0M5BHH0020WFY (Add a DLC to test the pack unlock and import).

## Scope

- Read the real pack CSV card names and the real committed `src/sprites/` + `src/card-art-map.json`.
- Mirror the existing art-agreement coverage in `tests/main-street/card-art.test.ts`.
- Tests only; no game code.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A Vitest suite derives every distinct card name from the residential pack CSV and asserts `hasDedicatedCardArt(name) === true` and `resolveCardArtName(name) !== CARD_ART_FALLBACK` for each.

- The suite asserts the pre-existing base-card art coverage/aliases are unchanged (no regression/churn from regeneration).
- The suite is expected to be red until the pack-art child lands, then green with no further test edits.

## Minimal Implementation

- New `tests/main-street/ResidentialPackArt.test.ts`, reusing the CSV-name and embedded-bitmap helpers from `card-art.test.ts`.

- `src/MainStreetCardArt.ts`, `src/card-art-map.json`, `src/sprites/` — Read.

## Deliverables

# Verification: pack unlock, purchase & save/load pipeline

**Summary:** Author the end-to-end verification that a locked residential pack stays out of play, a scoped simulated purchase unlocks **only** it, the pack merges and deals, saves round-trip it, and a missing/disabled pack degrades gracefully — including the browser-level listing behaviour.

**Parent:** MS-0MV0M5BHH0020WFY (Add a DLC to test the pack unlock and import).

## Scope

- Extend the real-content-directory pipeline pattern from `tests/main-street/CardPackPipelineIntegration.test.ts` to the production pack.
- Drive the real core action-reward service/store with an in-memory store (no Electron).
- Cover both unit (Node/Vitest) and browser (Chromium) layers; browser files run under the `browser` Vitest project.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A unit suite materialises the production pack into a temp `<contentDir>/packs/` and asserts the gate is **locked** when no `dlc:main-street:main-street-residential-pack` unlock exists, and that the pack's card ids are absent from the merged pool and live templates.
- The suite asserts a scoped simulated purchase (the configured dev/QA rule requesting only the residential target) flips the pack to **unlocked**, that it can then be enabled, and that its card ids appear in the merged pool and are dealt by the game.
- The suite asserts the scoped purchase unlocks **only** the residential pack and does **not** unlock the configured itch.io golf reward (`itchio-follow`), and that a global `refresh({ attested: true })` does not unlock the residential pack.
- The suite asserts save → reset → load round-trips the active residential pack, the merged pool checksum and the cards in play, and that a missing/disabled pack degrades to base content with a warning (refusing to resume only when a live instance needs a missing template).
- A browser suite asserts the Card Packs listing shows the residential pack **locked**, the simulated-purchase control flips it to **unlocked**, and it is then enable-able.
- The suites are expected to be red until the gate, purchase and listing children land, then green with no further test edits.

## Minimal Implementation

- New `tests/main-street/ResidentialPackPipelineIntegration.test.ts` (unit) extending the existing pipeline helpers.

# Production residential pack content & builder wrapper

**Summary:** Author the shipped production residential card pack under a new top-level `packs/` directory and wire a Main Street npm wrapper around the core card-pack builder so it builds reproducibly into an installable `<contentDir>/packs/` root.

**Parent:** MS-0MV0M5BHH0020WFY (Add a DLC to test the pack unlock and import).

## Scope

- New production content only; purely additive (no base `card-data.csv` or balance changes).
- Pack id / DLC id: `main-street-residential-pack`; `gameId`: `main-street`.
- Reuse the core pack contract, builder and merge seam — no bespoke build logic.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `packs/manifest.json` declares the `main-street-residential-pack` entry (`gameId: main-street`, version, `coreEngineVersion` range, `cards`, `assets`) alongside the reference pack catalogue shape.
- `packs/main-street/main-street-residential-pack/cards.csv` reuses Main Street's `src/card-data.csv` header **exactly** and adds 8–12 residential-themed cards spanning the families (business, event, upgrade, staff, community-space), with unique ids and no id/name collision with the base pool; rows follow the existing tier/cost/effect conventions.
- `packs/main-street/main-street-residential-pack/assets/` contains the pack art assets, and `packs/README.md` documents authoring, building and installing the pack.

# Bespoke residential pack art & generator coverage

**Summary:** Produce bespoke, deterministic, licence-clean 1024×1024 source sprites for every residential pack card and extend the art-map generator so pack card names are mapped and resolve to dedicated (non-`Fallback`) art in the regenerated `src/card-art-map.json`.

**Parent:** MS-0MV0M5BHH0020WFY (Add a DLC to test the pack unlock and import).

## Scope

- One bespoke sprite per new pack card, committed under `src/sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`.
- Art is project-generated and reproducible; base card art output must not regress.
- Small pack-art assets under `packs/main-street/main-street-residential-pack/assets/` are owned by the content child; this child owns the card-face source sprites and the generated map.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A committed, deterministic generator produces the pack card sprites (`src/sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`) reproducibly (identical input → byte-identical output) using the existing `sharp` dependency; the art is project-owned (CC0) and contains no third-party content.

- The runtime resolver (`resolveCardArtName`/`hasDedicatedCardArt`) and the static SVG generator resolve every pack card to the same dedicated sprite.
- Regeneration leaves the existing base-card aliases/art entries unchanged apart from the additive pack entries.

- New `src/scripts/generate-residential-pack-art.mjs`: deterministic SVG→PNG (or equivalent vector) art for the pack cards via `sharp`, with a fixed seed/palette per card.

# Content-unlock pack entitlement gate

**Summary:** Compose Main Street's pack entitlement resolution so a `dlc:main-street:main-street-residential-pack` unlock in the launcher's unified content-unlock store entitles the pack **in addition to** the existing Steam-DLC status, while an unowned pack stays locked and out of play.

**Parent:** MS-0MV0M5BHH0020WFY (Add a DLC to test the pack unlock and import).

## Scope

- Read side only: compose the content-unlock client into the `CardPackLoaderOptions.resolveEntitlement` seam used by `loadMainStreetCardPacks`.
- Do not change the core loader's default behaviour or other games' entitlement.
- Reuse the core `content-unlock-client` (`contentUnlockClientFromWindow`) and, where useful, the pure `DlcGate`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `loadMainStreetCardPacks` composes an entitlement resolver that reports a pack **unlocked** when a `dlc:<gameId>:<packId>` content unlock exists, in addition to the existing Steam-DLC status.
- With no content unlock the residential pack resolves **locked** with an actionable reason and its rows stay out of the merged pool; with the unlock it resolves **unlocked** and its rows merge.
- Only packs declared as content-unlock gated are affected; entitlement for every other pack and game is unchanged.
- The composition is total (never throws): a missing, throwing or malformed content-unlock bridge degrades to the Steam status / base content.
- The gating declaration is data-driven (a pack/manifest or game-config declaration), not a hard-coded pack title in logic.

## Minimal Implementation

- Add an optional `contentUnlocks` client (defaulting to `contentUnlockClientFromWindow()`) and a composed `resolveEntitlement` in `src/MainStreetCardPacks.ts` (or a new focused `src/MainStreetContentUnlockGate.ts` module).
- Determine which pack ids are content-unlock gated from an explicit declaration (proposed: an additive `entitlement` marker surfaced on `CardPackStatusRef`; record the final shape as an assumption if it differs).
- Extend `tests/main-street/MainStreetCardPacks.test.ts` seam coverage in the pipeline verification child.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/MainStreetCardPacks.ts` — Compose content-unlock entitlement into the loader seam.
- `src/MainStreetContentUnlockGate.ts` — New (optional) focused resolver.
- `core/src/ui/content-unlock-client.ts`, `core/src/core-engine/DlcGate.ts` — Read/reuse.
- `core/src/ui/CardPackLoader.ts` — `resolveEntitlement` seam (read; additive ref shape only if required).

## Dependencies

- Verified by **Verification: pack unlock, purchase & save/load pipeline**.
- Blocks **Card Packs listing simulated-purchase affordance** (the listing must render the locked → unlocked transition).

## Deliverables

- A total, data-driven content-unlock composition at the pack entitlement seam, with the gating declaration documented.

# Scoped simulated purchase in the core launcher

**Summary:** Add a config-driven, rule-scoped simulated purchase to the core launcher's unified content-unlock mechanism so a dev/QA affordance can unlock the residential pack's DLC target without collateral-unlocking other rewards (notably the itch.io golf reward).

**Parent:** MS-0MV0M5BHH0020WFY (Add a DLC to test the pack unlock and import).

## Scope

- Write path (main process + renderer read client) in the `./core` submodule; commit there and bump the submodule pointer in this work item.
- Keep the change additive and config-driven (no hard-coded game/DLC names in logic).
- Must not weaken the existing `steam-follow` self-attest path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `core/electron/action-rewards.json` gains a config rule whose target is `dlc:main-street:main-street-residential-pack`, triggered by a dev/QA `(platform, action)` pair resolved to a simulated-purchase verifier.
- `ActionRewardService.refresh` accepts an additive rule-scope filter and an explicit simulated-purchase signal, forwarded to `ActionVerificationRequest`; a scoped refresh evaluates only the named rule(s) and never self-attests unrelated rules.
- A `SimulatedPurchaseVerifier` (or equivalent) verifies **only** when a simulated purchase is explicitly requested, so a global `refresh({ attested: true })` cannot unlock the residential pack.
- The `contentUnlocks:refresh` IPC handler and preload bridge carry the scoped request, and the renderer `ContentUnlockClient` exposes a typed `refresh` call (the existing `isUnlocked`/`getUnlocks` API is unchanged).
- Tests prove a scoped residential purchase unlocks the residential DLC and does **not** unlock the configured `itchio-follow` golf reward, and that global attestation does not unlock the residential pack.
- The core change is committed to `./core` and the submodule bumped in the same work item; both commit hashes are recorded.

## Minimal Implementation

- Extend `ActionRewardRefreshOptions` (`ruleIds?`, `simulatePurchase?`) and `ActionVerificationRequest` (`simulatePurchase?`) in `core/electron/action-rewards.ts` / `action-verifiers.ts`.
- Add `SimulatedPurchaseVerifier` (id `simulated-purchase`) and register it in `initContentUnlocks` (`core/electron/main.ts`) with the config's verifier mapping.
- Normalise `ruleIds`/`simulatePurchase` in `core/electron/action-rewards-ipc.ts`; pass through `core/electron/preload.cjs`; add `refresh()` to `core/src/ui/content-unlock-client.ts`.
- Add the rule + `verifiers.actions` entry to `core/electron/action-rewards.json` (validated against `core/electron/bonus-catalog.json`, where `main-street` is already registered).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `core/electron/action-rewards.json` — New residential-pack purchase rule + verifier mapping.
- `core/electron/action-rewards.ts` — Rule-scope filter + simulated-purchase signal.
- `core/electron/action-verifiers.ts` — `SimulatedPurchaseVerifier`.
- `core/electron/action-rewards-ipc.ts`, `core/electron/preload.cjs` — Scoped refresh transport.
- `core/src/ui/content-unlock-client.ts` — Typed `refresh`.
- `core/electron/main.ts` — Register the verifier.
- `core/tests/electron/**` — New/extended unit coverage.

## Dependencies

- Verified by **Verification: pack unlock, purchase & save/load pipeline**.
- Blocks **Card Packs listing simulated-purchase affordance** (the affordance calls the scoped purchase).

## Deliverables

- Committed core change + submodule bump, with scoping proven by tests.

# Card Packs listing simulated-purchase affordance

**Summary:** Add a dev/QA affordance in the in-game Card Packs panel that performs the scoped simulated purchase for the residential pack, refreshes the pack pool, and lets the player enable the newly unlocked pack.

**Parent:** MS-0MV0M5BHH0020WFY (Add a DLC to test the pack unlock and import).

## Scope

- UI-only change in Main Street plus an additive action seam on the reusable core `CardPackListing`.
- No animation (honours reduced motion by construction); plays the standard UI SFX.
- Inert in a plain browser with no content-unlock bridge.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The Card Packs panel renders a simulated-purchase control on the **locked** residential pack row (additive `onPurchase`/row-action seam on `CardPackListing`); the control is only offered for content-unlock-gated packs.
- Activating it performs the scoped purchase through the renderer content-unlock client, re-runs pack discovery (`loadMainStreetCardPacks`/`bootstrapMainStreetCardPacks`) and re-renders the listing, so the pack shows **unlocked** and is enable-able.
- Enabling the newly unlocked pack merges its rows and its cards deal in play; the enabled set persists as the new-game preference via the existing `applyEnabledMainStreetPacks` path.
- With no content-unlock bridge (plain browser) the affordance is a no-op and the listing still renders without error; the interaction plays `COMMON_SFX_KEYS.UI_CLICK`.
- Keeps SLL layout (no hard-coded pixel coordinates) and a browser test covers locked → purchase → unlocked → enabled.

## Minimal Implementation

- Add an optional `onPurchase` callback/row action to `core/src/ui/CardPackListing.ts`.
- Wire `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` `showCardPacksDialog` to call the scoped refresh, re-discover and update `listing.setResult(...)`.
- Add a Main Street helper (e.g. `purchaseMainStreetCardPack(packId)`) wrapping the content-unlock client refresh for testability.
